newsitem.title: USA: U.S. milk prices at 6-year low, more falls seen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. milk prices at 6-year low, more falls seen.

text.p: U.S. milk producer prices in the April-June quarter of 1997 were the lowest in six years and more declines are likely in the second half of the year, the Dairy and Food Market Analyst said in a weekly update.

The Basic Formula Price averaged $10.96 in the second quarter, compared with an average $12.01 the previous seven years, the newsletter said. "Our second half outlook calls for milk prices at least $1 below historical levels in the third quarter but rebounding above historical levels in the fourth."
Manufacturers paid a few cents more for milk in June, leaving the June BFP at $10.74, up 4 cents from May.
"We don't expect milk prices to start moving higher until August," said the newsletter, which projects the August BFP at $11.35 and the September BFP at $12.20.
"Based on current conditions, we believe butter prices will hold steady over the next month while cheese prices cold begin inching up by the end of the month," it said.
"However, as the composition of milk weakens over the next two months, Grade B plants will pay 10/20 cents per CWT less for milk," it added.

The newsletter said demand for cheese is still soft in all market channels. Barrels are particularly long and Western cheese is readily available, putting downward pressure on prices east of the Rockies, it said. Barrels continue moving to CCC under their support program.

Heat in the Midwest and Northeast had begun to trim milk production and dampen solids content in milk, reducing cheese yields. Milk was being pulled from New Mexico to the Souhteast to meet processing needs, the newsletter said.
Barrels were quoted at 112.25 cents a lb and blocks at 116.75 cents on Friday at the Chicago Cheese Exchnage.
Butter prices held steady for a fifth straight week, with AA quoted at 113.00 cents a lb at the Chicago Butter Exchange.
